source.scope: Source-aligned arguments for incomplete and consistent_unprovable. The first expands the self-substitution proof. The second expands the generic provability argument and its arithmetic instantiation.

nodes.name: LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete
nodes.lean: theorem incomplete (T : ArithmeticTheory) [T.Δ₁] [𝗥₀ ⪯ T] [T.SoundOnHierarchy 𝚺 1] : Incomplete T

nodes.name: Rule out a proof of G
Reduce a proof of consistency to G

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.title: First incompleteness theorem
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.summary: A Δ₁-presented, Σ₁-sound arithmetic theory at least as strong as R₀ leaves a sentence and its negation unprovable.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.why_here: The proof concludes incompleteness by exhibiting an undecided sentence.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.title: Second incompleteness theorem
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.summary: A consistent Δ₁-presented arithmetic theory at least as strong as IΣ₁ cannot prove its standard consistency sentence.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.why_here: The arithmetic theorem specializes the generic result to the standard provability predicate of T.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.title: Σ₁ and recursive enumerability
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.summary: A predicate on natural numbers is recursively enumerable exactly when it has a Σ₁ definition.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.why_here: The proof applies this characterization to establish recursive enumerability of D.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.title: Standard provability structure
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.summary: The arithmetic provability predicate is packaged as a reusable provability structure.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.why_here: The construction step unfolds this definition to obtain the arithmetic provability predicate.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.title: Internal consistency sentence
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.summary: The standard consistency assertion is a Π₁ sentence asserting that no proof of contradiction exists.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.why_here: The consistency-sentence step unfolds this definition.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.title: Positive introspection
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.summary: The third derivability condition comes from arithmetic Σ₁-completeness.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.why_here: The graph includes D3 in its summary of the derivability conditions.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.title: Represent recursively enumerable predicates
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.summary: The representability result connects membership of n in an enumerated predicate to provability of the coded numeral instance.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.why_here: The representation step applies this result to D.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.title: Gödel sentence specification
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.summary: The diagonalization theorem produces a formula equivalent to its own unprovability in the base theory.
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.why_here: The diagonalization step summarizes this fixed-point result.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.title: Generic consistency unprovability
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.summary: The generic second incompleteness result derives a proof of G from a hypothetical proof of Con(T).
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.why_here: The graph summarizes this theorem by reducing a proof of consistency to a proof of G.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:presentation.title: Δ₁ presentation
fact:presentation.summary: The theory has the definable presentation assumed by both formalizations. This is a shared input schema for the two branches.
fact:presentation.why_here: It is a premise for defining D and forming standard provability.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:r0.title: Arithmetic base R₀
fact:r0.summary: The first proof assumes sufficient arithmetic strength for the representability argument.
fact:r0.why_here: The base extension is a premise for representing D by provability in T.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:soundness.title: Σ₁-sound theory
fact:soundness.summary: This is a hypothesis of the first theorem in the catalogue, sufficient in particular for metatheoretic consistency.
fact:soundness.why_here: The final diagonal argument uses soundness to rule out both derivations.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:isigma.title: Arithmetic base IΣ₁
fact:isigma.summary: The second theorem assumes this stronger arithmetic base for the standard provability machinery.
fact:isigma.why_here: The graph uses this base for standard provability, the derivability conditions, and the Gödel sentence.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:consistency.title: External consistency
fact:consistency.summary: The second theorem assumes metatheoretic consistency as a typeclass.
fact:consistency.why_here: External consistency is a premise for excluding a proof of G.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:define-D.title: Code refutation after substitution
step:define-D.summary: Define D on codes of one-variable formulas. A code qualifies when T proves the negation of that formula after self-substitution.
step:define-D.why_here: This introduces the predicate used in the enumerability and self-substitution arguments.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:define-D.title: The predicate D
fact:define-D.summary: D specifies which self-instantiated formulas are refutable in T.
fact:define-D.why_here: Its definition is used both to show enumerability and to identify the diagonal instance.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:enumerate-D.title: Show D is recursively enumerable
step:enumerate-D.summary: The definability tactic establishes a Σ₁ definition. Apply the equivalence between Σ₁ predicates and recursively enumerable predicates.
step:enumerate-D.why_here: This establishes the hypothesis needed for the representation step.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:enumerate-D.title: D is recursively enumerable
fact:enumerate-D.summary: D can be represented using the library’s enumeration machinery.
fact:enumerate-D.why_here: This makes the representation theorem applicable to D.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:represent-D.title: Represent D by a formula
step:represent-D.summary: Choose δ with codeOfREPred D and use re_complete to characterize when each numeral instance is provable.
step:represent-D.why_here: This supplies the formula later evaluated at its own code.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:represent-D.title: Provability represents D
fact:represent-D.summary: The representation is about provability in T, with n ranging over natural numbers.
fact:represent-D.why_here: The self-substitution step uses this characterization at the code of δ.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:self-substitute.title: Substitute δ’s own code
step:self-substitute.summary: Specializing the representation and the specification of D to δ yields equivalent provability of π and its negation.
step:self-substitute.why_here: The comparison yields equivalence of the external provability claims for the diagonal sentence and its negation.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:self-substitute.title: Opposite provability claims coincide
fact:self-substitute.summary: This is a metatheoretic equivalence between two provability claims.
fact:self-substitute.why_here: Any proof on either side would give proofs on both sides.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:exclude-both.title: Rule out both derivations
step:exclude-both.summary: Either proof would yield the opposite proof and contradict consistency. The soundness hypothesis supplies consistency.
step:exclude-both.why_here: The equivalence forces either proposed proof to yield a contradiction, so the sentence is undecided.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:exclude-both.title: An undecided sentence
fact:exclude-both.why_here: This sentence witnesses the first theorem’s incompleteness conclusion.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:standard-provability.title: Form standard provability
step:standard-provability.summary: Package the standard predicate, with the derivability conditions supplied by the arithmetic development.
step:standard-provability.why_here: This instantiates the predicate used for derivability, internal consistency, and diagonalization.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:standard-provability.title: Standard provability for T
fact:standard-provability.summary: The boxed formula expresses existence of a T-proof of the coded sentence.
fact:standard-provability.why_here: The same predicate enters the derivability conditions, consistency sentence, and Gödel sentence.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:hbl-conditions.title: Supply derivability conditions
step:hbl-conditions.summary: The standard structure internalizes derivations and supports internal modus ponens and positive introspection.
step:hbl-conditions.why_here: These conditions support the internal provability argument.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:hbl-conditions.title: Hilbert–Bernays–Löb structure
fact:hbl-conditions.summary: The generic provability result can be instantiated with the standard predicate.
fact:hbl-conditions.why_here: They let the base theory formalize the implication from the consistency sentence to internal unprovability of G.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:consistency-sentence.title: Express consistency internally
step:consistency-sentence.summary: Use the Π₁ sentence formed by negating internal provability of absurdity.
step:consistency-sentence.why_here: This provides the sentence whose provability the second argument investigates.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:consistency-sentence.title: Internal Con(T)
fact:consistency-sentence.summary: This is a sentence of arithmetic, usable inside a judgment about T-provability.
fact:consistency-sentence.why_here: It appears as the antecedent of the internal implication about G.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:godel-sentence.title: Diagonalize the provability predicate
step:godel-sentence.summary: Apply diagonalization to the negated standard proof predicate. Here the base theory T₀ is IΣ₁.
step:godel-sentence.why_here: The resulting sentence is used in both the external and internal unprovability arguments.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:godel-sentence.title: A Gödel sentence for T
fact:godel-sentence.summary: The equivalence is a theorem inside the arithmetic base, with G separate from the witness used by the first theorem on this page.
fact:godel-sentence.why_here: The fixed-point equivalence supports the proof of external unprovability and the internal equivalence with Con(T).

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:godel-unprovable.title: Rule out a proof of G
step:godel-unprovable.summary: A proof of G internalizes as a proof of □G via D1. The Gödel equivalence gives ¬□G from G, contradicting external consistency.
step:godel-unprovable.why_here: This establishes the external unprovability later transferred to Con(T).

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:godel-unprovable.title: External unprovability of G
fact:godel-unprovable.summary: This unprovability claim is made in the metatheory.
fact:godel-unprovable.why_here: It rules out the proof of G that would follow from a proof of Con(T).

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:internal-unprovability.title: Formalize the implication
step:internal-unprovability.summary: Use positive introspection, internalized consequences of the Gödel equivalence, and internal modus ponens to derive that □G entails □⊥. Take its contrapositive.
step:internal-unprovability.why_here: This supplies the implication used to connect Con(T) to G.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:internal-unprovability.title: Internal implication
fact:internal-unprovability.summary: The base theory proves that consistency implies the unprovability of the Gödel sentence.
fact:internal-unprovability.why_here: Combining this implication with the fixed-point specification gives the direction from Con(T) to G.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:equate-godel-consistency.title: Relate G to consistency
step:equate-godel-consistency.summary: For the reverse direction, any proof of contradiction would prove G, so its internal unprovability implies internal consistency. Combine both directions with the Gödel sentence equivalence.
step:equate-godel-consistency.why_here: The implication from Con(T) to G transfers a hypothetical proof of Con(T) to G.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:equate-godel-consistency.title: Gödel sentence equivalent to consistency
fact:equate-godel-consistency.summary: The equivalence is provable at the arithmetic base and transfers to T.
fact:equate-godel-consistency.why_here: The generic argument uses the direction from Con(T) to G.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

step:generic-unprovability.title: Reduce a proof of consistency to G
step:generic-unprovability.summary: Because the base theory is weaker than T, a hypothetical T-proof of its consistency would yield a T-proof of G. This contradicts the earlier external unprovability result.
step:generic-unprovability.why_here: This derives the generic conclusion later instantiated for arithmetic.

provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

fact:generic-unprovability.title: T cannot prove Con(T)
fact:generic-unprovability.summary: The final arithmetic theorem specializes this generic lemma to the standard provability structure.
fact:generic-unprovability.why_here: This generic conclusion yields the second arithmetic theorem.

concepts.title: Arithmetized provability
concepts.summary: Represent syntax and proof existence by predicates on Gödel codes so that arithmetic can reason about proofs.

concepts.title: Diagonal self-substitution
concepts.summary: Insert the numeral for a formula’s own code as its argument, producing a sentence with a provability relationship to itself.

annotation_provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

concepts.title: Consistency and soundness
concepts.summary: Consistency rules out an external derivation of contradiction. Σ₁-soundness additionally controls which Σ₁ sentences the theory can prove.

annotation_provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

concepts.title: Hilbert–Bernays–Löb conditions
concepts.summary: Standard provability internalizes proofs, distributes over implication and supports positive introspection.

annotation_provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

groups.title: Represent the refutation predicate
groups.summary: Show that D is recursively enumerable and represent it in arithmetic.

annotation_provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

groups.title: Diagonalize and use consistency
groups.summary: Turn representation into opposite provability claims, then rule both out.

annotation_provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

groups.title: Properties of standard provability
groups.summary: Certify the derivability conditions and encode consistency.

annotation_provenance.author: Codex CLI (ChatGPT) with source-reviewed display annotations

groups.title: Relate consistency to the Gödel sentence
groups.summary: Prove the equivalence in the base theory.
